clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following year: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and distanced himself from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and his marriage separated; your mother's anxiety rose over Anton; your brother Callum had ear infections; your grandmother took a job at the library and her functioning came back. The shifts pile up from February through May 1979, and no one else's shows then.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest in March 1984, within six months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house and overfunctioned; your father argued with his mother over how the house was kept; your brother Callum stammered again; your sister Ines was born in September. The shifts beside these events show a tightening in the household around your mother's loss of functioning and your grandmother's move to manage the home.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, over the following decade: your grandfather Ambrose overfunctioned with her care; your father phoned his father every night in anxiety; your grandmother had a fall and her functioning fell; your father and uncle Lyle argued over who should help; your grandfather had chest pains; your grandmother's functioning fell again in 1991 and 1995; your mother overfunctioned with her clinic visits; your aunt Mavis came to nurse her; your father drank most evenings and fought with your mother over his evenings at his parents' house. The shifts show a slow climb from 1986, each step a new strain, with no settling between them until your grandmother moved to the nursing home in 1997.

clusters.name: Callum's leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving for work up north in May 1999, within eighteen months: your father and Callum argued over his plans; your mother's anxiety rose and she could not settle; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage, his functioning fell; your sister Ines skipped school through the autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere; Ines's functioning came back and she passed her exams by August 2000. The shifts show your father's move away and your mother's pull toward Ines, side by side.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within ten months: you could not sleep more than a few hours; you stopped going to the bookshop and lost the job in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; by November you took a job at the garden centre and your sleeping came back. The shifts are yours alone in these months, and no one else's shows then.
